title: Outlook for Gig and Platform Workers and Measures to Help Enhance Their Employability and CPF Savings
what_it_is: Outlook for Gig and Platform Workers and Measures to Help Enhance Their Employability and CPF Savings

sections.label: Gig worker CPF and job outlook
sections.summary: Questions ask what concerns platform companies and gig workers raised on mandatory CPF contributions, whether a survey was done, and the job outlook for food delivery riders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what are the concerns that platform companies and gig workers have raised with respect to the suggestion for platform companies to make mandatory CPF contributions for gig workers; (b) whether a survey or poll has been conducted to determine the proportion of gig workers who support such a suggestion; and (c) if so, what are the survey results.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what is the longer-term job outlook for food delivery riders; and (b) whether there is a need to improve the employability and career planning for food delivery riders.

sections.label: Support for mandatory CPF contributions
sections.summary: More than half of submissions touched on CPF contributions, and 55% of those indicated support for mandatory CPF contributions to platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: To Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman’s question, more than half of these submissions touched on CPF contributions, of which, 55% indicated support for the idea of mandatory CPF contributions to platform workers.

sections.label: IPS study on delivery riders
sections.summary: An IPS ethnographic study found riders wanting over $4,000 monthly would likely work over 10 hours daily, six to seven days weekly, cycling 60 to 70 kilometres.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: An independent ethnographic study by the Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) on delivery riders found that riders who are keen to earn an income of more than $4,000 a month would likely need to work more than 10 hours a day, for six to seven days a week, cycling at least 60 kilometres to 70 kilometres a day and not reject any assigned orders.

sections.label: Committee recommendations and phase-in period
sections.summary: The Committee aims to give practicable and sustainable recommendations and is considering an appropriate phase-in period for the industry to adjust.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The Committee aims to provide practicable and sustainable recommendations and is considering an appropriate phase-in period to allow the industry to adjust.

sections.label: Demographics of 8% transition
sections.summary: On the demographics of the 8% who may have made the transition, the speaker says he does not have the full data.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: I think we need to look at this from a multi-pronged perspective.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Therefore, in answer to the first question posed, on what are the demographics of the 8% who may have made the transition, I do not have the full data.

sections.label: CPF contribution data assessment
sections.summary: Data is being sought from CPF and platform companies, but the assessment is that around 45% or thereabout are making some CPF contributions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: We are trying to get data from CPF and the platform companies to see if we can get a better sense of it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But our assessment is that probably around 45% or thereabout, are making some CPF contributions.

sections.label: Phasing in CPF contributions
sections.summary: The Committee asks if MOM would phase in platform company CPF contributions to cushion price and take-home income impacts, and will engage companies and workers before recommending.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Would MOM also consider phasing in CPF contributions by platform companies to cushion any price impact on consumers and alleviate any potential adverse impact on the take-home income of our platform workers, which is something that the Labour Movement is, ultimately, the most worried about?

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: That is probably one way to actually ease the industry into this transition of some CPF contribution, so that the immediate impact on both consumers, platform workers and the business costs of the companies can be managed over time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: This is something that the Committee will engage further with the companies and the workers before landing on a fixed recommendation.
